user_requirements: ROUND 4 — focused review of the NEW client-protection layer in a legal draft (not an acquisition analysis). SPA_DRAFT_V6.md is v6 of the share sale agreement; deal_facts.txt (READ FIRST, especially the CLIENT-PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS section at the end) records the purchaser's three new requirements and how v6 implements them (new cl 4.5; new cl 11.4-11.6; consequential edits to 11.2, 14.4, 15.1). ROUND3_FINAL_READTHROUGH.md records the previously cleared v4/v5 state. Your job, in priority order: (1) REQUIREMENT FIDELITY — do cl 4.5, 11.4, 11.5 and 11.6 implement the purchaser's three requirements exactly and completely: the ASG-only liaison role but both-companies good-faith duty; the 2-month client-retention protection with causation limited to matters 'directly contributed to in any capacity' by the Vendor; the no-client-contact-without-written-confirmation rule? Quote any divergence. (2) ENFORCEABILITY AND FAIRNESS — stress-test cl 11.6 in particular: is a client-departure set-off trigger with 'directly contributed to' causation defensible, or does it drift toward making the Vendor an insurer of client retention (penalty risk)? Is the burden of proof workable? Does the interaction of 11.6 with 15.1's own 'material breach' + reasonable-estimate machinery double-count or conflict? (3) INTERACTIONS — cl 11.5 no-contact vs cl 9.4 advisory role (QC/compliance is team-facing, but could QC site visits involve incidental client contact at venues?); cl 11.5 vs 11.1(a)/(c) (overlap or conflict?); cl 4.5 good-faith duty vs the Vendor's existing employment duties pre-settlement (does it conflict with the s149 employment-matters-only design of cl 9.2?); the Client Protection Period definition vs the 24-month restraints (should be complementary layers, not a 2-month cap on anything); cl 14.4 override reaches the new clauses. (4) DRAFTING QUALITY — placement of the definitions (11.4 inside the non-solicitation clause), numbering, cross-references, any residual issue. Output: requirement-fidelity verdict per requirement, findings with severity (BLOCKER/RECOMMENDED/OPTIONAL) and exact fix wording, final sign-readiness verdict.
acquirer_context: Purchaser-side review. The Vendor is the current ASG client liaison staying on post-settlement as advisor (QC/compliance of the team) under a separate agreement. Deferred consideration $100k/$80k/$80k with set-off; the new client-protection layer exists because the client relationships are the asset most at risk in the instalment window. Same regulatory-integrity constraint as all prior rounds (open PSPLA/CIPU process — nothing may fetter regulator communications). The final document goes to Franklin Law.
